name: Reel
text: Adopt the dual-device setup: pair the $300 TPM-backed NVMe (Samsung PM1743) with the $50 PCIe validator running open firmware. This forces both devices to agree on every write, eliminating single points of failure—drive firmware, host stack, and bus can’t lie without detection. The trade-off is higher cost ($350) and setup complexity, but it’s the only way to remove all software and hardware trust assumptions at once.

name: Scriv
text: The $200 Raspberry Pi CM5 validator still trusts *its* firmware—Coreboot and Linux IMA can be backdoored or misconfigured. The real fix is a *hardware-rooted validator* with a write-once log: use a $150 Lattice iCE40 FPGA + NVMe HAT running open-source firmware (e.g., LiteX) to enforce Merkle proofs at the hardware level. That’s the only way to remove all firmware trust.
